children: U.S. natural gas futures start the week lower with the market bracing for cooler late-September weather that will reduce power-sector demand. "Cooling demand is expected to step down steadily through the second half of September, making today's decline look more like a repricing of near-term weather exposure than a sharp deterioration in fundamentals," Gelber & Associates says in a note. Strong LNG demand remains the strongest counterweight to bearish weather, the firm adds. Nymex natural gas settles down 2% at $2.916/mmBtu. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
